plans: Hypothesis: the strict and permissive pair expressions both use a greedy name class that overlaps following whitespace, so a long whitespace-heavy prefix with no equals sign forces many name/whitespace split attempts and quadratic event-loop CPU use. Prerequisites: read access to the parser source, a local JavaScript runtime, disposable source copies, and untrusted Set-Cookie text reaching the public parse entry point; permissive mode is opt-in and ordinary cookies are available as controls. Bounded test: time parsing 'a'.repeat(n) + ' '.repeat(n) + '!' for n = 2000 through 64000 in both modes with a median of three and a fixed external timeout, compare with a no-whitespace malformed cookie and an early-equals value tail, and add a semicolon-plus-attribute variant to exclude later stages; then replace both pair expressions with a deterministic left-to-right separator scan and re-run the same matrix plus a strict/permissive semantic differential. Expected support: about fourfold growth per doubling before the repair and near-linear growth after, with zero field changes on ordinary, quoted, empty-name, leading and multiple equals, terminator, attribute, and trailing-semicolon cases. Falsifier: before the repair, flat timing or only one mode affected; after the repair, any key, value, or attribute change or more than roughly twofold growth per doubling. Cleanup and limitation: delete disposable fixtures and keep the differential corpus; one input family and one machine do not prove universal equivalence, and a separate attribute-loop sink may remain.

Length-bound-at-entry: keep the existing pair expressions but reject Set-Cookie strings above a small maximum length, optionally after a cheap presence check for an equals sign. Hypothesis: real cookie headers are small, so a boundary cap removes the practical CPU sink with a tiny patch. Test the same timing and semantic matrices plus boundary values just below and above the cap. Expected support: capped inputs return quickly and ordinary cookies are unchanged. Falsifier: a legitimate large cookie stops parsing, or inputs just below the cap still show superlinear delay. Limitation: this caps the resource rather than removing the quadratic match.

Disjoint-regex-classes: retain regular-expression parsing but make the name class exclude whitespace, or otherwise make the name and whitespace alternatives disjoint, so the engine cannot reconsider every split before a missing equals sign. Test strict and permissive modes on whitespace-heavy no-separator strings, then differential-test a broad accepted/rejected cookie corpus against the original parser. Expected support: timing becomes near-linear and all corpus outputs match. Falsifier: a name that legitimately contains internal whitespace changes behavior, or the rewritten expression still scales superlinearly.

Single-precomputed-split: compute the first equals-sign position once, slice a bounded name and value, and apply the existing pair expression only to the short slices, or bypass it for the pair split. Keep the attribute parser untouched. Test the quadratic fixture, the semantic corpus, and a differential comparison against the original parser on randomized short strings. Expected support: the expensive backtracking surface disappears because the expression no longer sees the long whitespace run, and attribute handling is unchanged. Falsifier: permissive leading-equals or multiple-equals cases differ from the original, or long input remains slow.
